answer:
Under Irish UCITS rules, ETF status attaches to a **share class**, not automatically to every sub-fund or sibling class. The UCITS ETF identifier is used in the **name of the relevant listed ETF class** (and in its marketing/communications and regulatory disclosures); it is not a blanket label for an umbrella or mixed umbrella.

A sub-fund may contain both listed and unlisted classes. Identify the **sub-fund** by its sub-fund name, but identify the ETF only by the class that is admitted to trading and meets the ETF definition—typically by appending “UCITS ETF” to that class’s name. Do not call the whole sub-fund an ETF if it also has non-ETF classes, and do not label other sub-funds in the umbrella as ETFs merely because one sibling is an ETF.

Check the fund’s prospectus and official class naming: legal naming and disclosure should make the ETF class, rather than the wider structure, clear.
